newsitem.title: UK: British surrogate mum gives birth to grandchild.
newsitem.headline: British surrogate mum gives birth to grandchild.

text.p: A 52-year-old woman has given birth to her daughter's child to become Britain's first "surrogate granny", her family said on Saturday.

Edith Jones gave birth to a girl on Thursday evening in Darlington, northeast England. She had been implanted with two embryos grown from eggs from her daughter Suzanne which were fertilised by sperm from Suzanne's husband, Chris Langston.
Jones, who already has two other children apart from Suzanne as well as a two-year-old grandchild, stepped in after it was found her 22-year-old daughter had been born without a womb.
The 52-year-old had been through hormone therapy before the eggs were implanted by doctors at a private clinic. The clinic's ethics committee cleared the operation in advance.
A spokesman for the Darlington hospital where the baby -- called Caitlin -- was delivered said: "The whole family is delighted. Mrs Jones is recovering well from her operation."
Not everyone approved of the operation.
"This situation technically makes both the natural mother and the child of the same generation.
"It will surely cause considerable confusion to both children," a spokesman for the Catholic church in Britain told the Sunday Telegraph newspaper.
